plants.name: Nepenthes ventricosa
plants.tip: The most forgiving of the genus, but only rainwater will do. Tap minerals build up in the sphagnum and kill it.
plants.colour: Pale green pitchers waisted in the middle, with a glossy red peristome

plants.name: Nepenthes × ventrata
plants.tip: The starter Nepenthes. It pitchers in ordinary room air, which almost nothing else in the genus will do.
plants.colour: Light green pitchers flushed orange-red, on a fast-climbing vine

plants.name: Nepenthes × miranda
plants.tip: Grows fast and gets heavy. Hang it where spent pitchers can be cut away without dragging the vine down.
plants.colour: Large speckled cream and maroon pitchers with a broad striped peristome

plants.name: Nepenthes alata
plants.tip: Pitchers fail before leaves do. If new leaves keep arriving bare, raise the humidity before changing anything else.
plants.colour: Slim pale green pitchers flecked red, with a narrow winged front

plants.name: Nepenthes sanguinea
plants.tip: A highlander. It wants nights around ten degrees cooler than its days, or it stops making pitchers altogether.
plants.colour: Long cylindrical pitchers in deep red, orange or lime, depending on the clone

plants.name: Nepenthes maxima
plants.tip: Intermediate and adaptable, but it resents drying out. Keep the sphagnum damp to the touch at all times.
plants.colour: Tall pitchers marbled cream and purple-brown, peristome finely ribbed

plants.name: Nepenthes truncata
plants.tip: Leaves are enormous and slow to replace. Use a wide, shallow pot and leave the roots alone for years at a time.
plants.colour: Squat scarlet to maroon pitchers beneath broad, blunt-ended leaves

plants.name: Nepenthes rafflesiana
plants.tip: A lowlander. It wants warmth all year and sulks below eighteen degrees, so keep it off cold winter windowsills.
plants.colour: Bulbous lower pitchers, cream blotched purple, with a glossy striped peristome

plants.name: Nepenthes ampullaria
plants.tip: It lives on fallen leaf litter rather than insects, so shade and steady warm damp matter more than catching prey.
plants.colour: Rounded squat pitchers in green, or green speckled red, carpeting the pot base

plants.name: Nepenthes bicalcarata
plants.tip: The slowest and fussiest lowlander. Constant warmth and near-saturated air, or it simply stops growing.
plants.colour: Orange-red pitchers with two downward-pointing fangs under the lid

plants.name: Nepenthes gracilis
plants.tip: Small, quick and tolerant of hard light once settled. Raise the light in stages or the thin leaves scorch.
plants.colour: Small narrow pitchers, green through to near-black, on wiry stems

plants.name: Nepenthes mirabilis
plants.tip: The widest-ranging species and among the easiest lowlanders. Warmth and rainwater are most of what it asks for.
plants.colour: Slender green to red pitchers with a fringed lid margin

plants.name: Nepenthes khasiana
plants.tip: The only Indian Nepenthes and unusually cold-tolerant. It still will not take tap water for a season.
plants.colour: Green pitchers ageing to deep red, with a narrow red peristome

plants.name: Nepenthes spectabilis
plants.tip: Highland Sumatran. Cool nights bring the dark colour out, and a warm still room loses it again.
plants.colour: Purple-black speckled pitchers with a pale striped peristome

plants.name: Nepenthes glabrata
plants.tip: A cool grower that hates heat. Above thirty degrees it declines fast, so keep it out of a summer conservatory.
plants.colour: Small white pitchers spotted red, with a yellow-green lid

plants.name: Nepenthes hamata
plants.tip: The hooked teeth only develop in cool, wet air. Highland conditions are not optional for this one.
plants.colour: Dark maroon pitchers with a black, hooked, comb-toothed peristome

plants.name: Nepenthes veitchii
plants.tip: Some forms climb by clasping bark flat against a trunk. Give it a slab or a stake rather than a hanging basket.
plants.colour: Broad golden-yellow banded peristome above a squat cream and red pitcher

plants.name: Nepenthes lowii
plants.tip: Difficult and slow. It needs genuinely cold nights, and the odd flared upper pitchers take years to appear.
plants.colour: Waisted, flared upper pitchers, green outside and deep red within

plants.name: Nepenthes rajah
plants.tip: Cool nights, lean open media and patience. Kept warm and stuffy the thick roots rot before you notice.
plants.colour: Huge low-slung maroon-purple pitchers with a heavily ribbed flared peristome

plants.name: Nepenthes villosa
plants.tip: Among the hardest in cultivation. Nights near ten degrees and living sphagnum, or it will not persist.
plants.colour: Globose pitchers with an extreme, deeply toothed orange-red peristome

plants.name: Nepenthes robcantleyi
plants.tip: Intermediate rather than true highland, and easier for it. The near-black colour only holds under strong light.
plants.colour: Very dark, almost black pitchers with a broad ribbed peristome

plants.name: Nepenthes singalana
plants.tip: A tough highlander that takes brighter light than most. It still wants a real temperature drop overnight.
plants.colour: Squat dark red pitchers with pale bands across the peristome

plants.name: Nepenthes tentaculata
plants.tip: Small, cool-growing and intolerant of dry air. A lit terrarium suits it far better than an open shelf.
plants.colour: Small speckled pitchers with bristly hairs on the upper surface of the lid

plants.name: Nepenthes fusca
plants.tip: Adaptable for a highlander and quick to climb. Cut the vine back and it throws basal shoots rather than sulking.
plants.colour: Narrow dark purple-brown pitchers with a slim toothed peristome

plants.name: Nepenthes aristolochioides
plants.tip: Rare and cool-growing. The domed shape only forms on mature growth, so young plants look unremarkable.
plants.colour: Domed, inflated pitchers with a small opening set at the front

plants.name: Nepenthes eymae
plants.tip: Highland Sulawesi. It makes ordinary lower pitchers for years before the funnel-shaped uppers arrive.
plants.colour: Funnel-shaped upper pitchers, pale yellow-green flushed pink

plants.name: Nepenthes ramispina
plants.tip: One of the easier highlanders. Strong light keeps the pitchers near-black, and shade fades them to green.
plants.colour: Slim near-black pitchers on dark wiry stems

plants.name: Nepenthes sibuyanensis
plants.tip: Intermediate and vigorous, and behind a lot of nursery hybrids. Keep the media open or the thick roots rot.
plants.colour: Squat pale pitchers with a very wide pink-red peristome

plants.name: Nepenthes northiana
plants.tip: A limestone-cliff plant. Growers often add a little crushed limestone, but warmth and damp matter more.
plants.colour: Large pale pitchers with a broad, strongly striped red peristome

plants.name: Nepenthes stenophylla
plants.tip: Intermediate and forgiving by highland standards. It climbs hard, so put a stake in early rather than late.
plants.colour: Long funnel pitchers, yellow-green speckled red, with a glossy banded peristome

plants.name: Nepenthes 'Bloody Mary'
plants.tip: A compact hybrid that colours hard in bright light and copes with ordinary room air rather than a terrarium.
plants.colour: Small squat pitchers in deep blood-red with a darker peristome

plants.name: Nepenthes 'Rebecca Soper'
plants.tip: Stays small enough for a windowsill. Strong light holds the red; a dim spot turns the pitchers plain green.
plants.colour: Small dark red pitchers with a fine pale peristome

plants.name: Nepenthes 'St. Gaya'
plants.tip: Sold widely as a beginner's plant. Rainwater and bright light are the two things it will not compromise on.
plants.colour: Green pitchers freckled red, with a red-striped peristome

plants.name: Nepenthes 'Rokko'
plants.tip: A tough nursery hybrid. It will pitcher in a bright bathroom without any enclosed case to hold the humidity.
plants.colour: Speckled cream and red pitchers on a robust vine

plants.name: Nepenthes 'Lady Luck'
plants.tip: The red is strongest on new pitchers in hard light. Older pitchers dull down, and that is age rather than a fault.
plants.colour: Rounded pitchers in a uniform deep red

plants.name: Nepenthes 'Bill Bailey'
plants.tip: A compact intermediate hybrid. Keep it damp and it pitchers steadily without needing cold highland nights.
plants.colour: Squat orange-red pitchers with a dark peristome

plants.name: Nepenthes 'Peter D'Amato'
plants.tip: Vigorous for a plant with so broad a peristome. Open, airy media and steady damp keep the roots sound.
plants.colour: Large pale pitchers with a wide, dark red, flared peristome

plants.name: Nepenthes 'Judith Finn'
plants.tip: Easier than either parent and keeps the broad toothed peristome. Steady intermediate temperatures throughout.
plants.colour: Squat red pitchers with a broad, banded, toothed peristome

plants.name: Nepenthes × hookeriana
plants.tip: A natural lowland hybrid. Warmth all year matters more than light, and cold wet roots in winter finish it.
plants.colour: Rounded pitchers, cream mottled maroon, midway between its two parents

plants.name: Nepenthes × trichocarpa
plants.tip: A vigorous small lowland hybrid. It takes more shade than most of the genus, but no cold at all.
plants.colour: Small green to red pitchers, narrow at the base and widening upward

plants.name: Nepenthes × dyeriana
plants.tip: A Victorian glasshouse hybrid still grown today. It wants the warm, wet air those houses were built to hold.
plants.colour: Long green pitchers heavily speckled maroon, with a striped peristome

plants.name: Nepenthes × coccinea
plants.tip: An old warm-growing hybrid, easy by the standards of the genus. Keep it above eighteen degrees all year.
plants.colour: Green pitchers washed and speckled scarlet
